title: vantridge alderwick video rebaseline
instruction:
You are the producer-director responsible for Vantridge Alliance’s training-video delivery to Alderwick Utilities. Eleven of the fourteen modules completed during the last two quarters were late, and Nikolai Rosenthal, Alderwick’s contract manager, has said service credits will begin next month unless he receives a credible revised schedule with a stated cause. Camila Reinholt has already told Alderwick informally that every remaining module will be delivered by the date quoted in her email, but the required editorial, accessibility and acceptance checks cannot simply be removed to make that date work. Use `Alderwick_video_delivery_evidence.xlsx`, which consolidates the project timestamps, suite and supplier bookings, correspondence, interview notes, contract milestones, working calendars and the release requirements for England and Scotland. The evidence leaves several explanations looking plausible: a single Alderwick subject expert gates script approvals, some asset handovers are incomplete, the outsourced colour grade is available only in blocks, and the review tool has dropped comment threads. I need the record to distinguish the cause of the slippage from conditions that merely resemble or amplify it. Prepare `Alderwick_rebaseline_and_variance.docx` as a combined re-baselined delivery schedule and concise variance memo for Brigid Alcantara and the operations team. It must show what is changing, when the remaining work can pass each material gate, who owns those gates, how the England and Scotland release paths differ, and whether the revised timing is being presented as an internal forecast or a client commitment. Include a workable control path for cases where an approval, asset handover, review record or supplier step cannot be completed as planned rather than assuming every handoff succeeds. Keep the document to no more than five pages, use only figures and commitments supported by the attachment, and present the schedule and its implications as facts rather than an options paper or recommendation. Write the file into the top level of the working directory using exactly the filename `Alderwick_rebaseline_and_variance.docx`.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/Alderwick_video_delivery_evidence.xlsx` — Consolidated source for historical module timestamps, future work, baseline milestones, calendars, bookings, correspondence, interview evidence, contractual definitions and England and Scotland release requirements.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `Alderwick_rebaseline_and_variance.docx` — A presentation-ready re-baselined delivery schedule and variance memo for the operations team. (Write the file at the top level of the working directory.; Use exactly the filename Alderwick_rebaseline_and_variance.docx.; Do not exceed five rendered pages.; Use only figures and commitments supported by the supplied evidence.; Cover both England and Scotland release paths.; Present one explicit interpretation of delivery and use it consistently.; Present facts and an executable schedule without making a recommendation.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

Causal finding. The repeated critical-path condition is the single Alderwick subject-expert approval queue: on every late module it waits after script readiness before edit can start, consuming float and propagating into accepted-master dates. The activity chain, not the number of incidents, supports that finding. Partial asset receipts affected AU-05, AU-09 and AU-12 but were completed before script work became controlling. Northline’s block availability amplified late approval on AU-07 and AU-11 by moving grade to the next booked block; it did not create the recurring initial wait. Dropped review threads on AU-08 and AU-12 were reconstructed from email and did not move their recorded accepted-master dates: they are an audit/rework control failure, not the recurring variance cause.

Vantridge producer; Alderwick subject expert

Review record: export comments to the module issue log; producer reconciles every comment and obtains reviewer acknowledgement before the next gate.
Vantridge producer
A vanished thread is a missing record, not approval; the signed reconciliation is the gate evidence.
Supplier control: confirm Northline module allocation before edit completes.
Vantridge post supervisor
Booking block and two-module capacity are entered in the control log.

spec.professional_context: Vantridge Alliance is re-baselining a troubled regional video programme for Alderwick Utilities before contractual service credits begin. Operations needs a defensible schedule that separates causal delay from coincident production problems and can be run when a normal handoff fails.
difficulty_sources: Distinguishing a recurring critical-path cause from three plausible but non-controlling production problems.
Reconstructing and calculating a feasible multi-gate schedule from timestamps, calendars, capacity and block bookings.
Choosing and consistently applying one of two supportable meanings of delivery.
Handling an informal promise without bypassing mandatory quality and acceptance controls.
Integrating different England and Scotland release paths into one concise operational document.

content_requirements: Provide a clean consolidated module register containing jurisdiction, contractual baseline milestones, actual milestone dates for completed work, status and remaining scope.
Provide timestamped activity evidence for asset handover, script readiness, client subject-expert approval, edit, colour grade, review, jurisdiction-specific release checks and acceptance.
Provide suite and outsourced supplier availability, working calendars, standard activity durations, dependency rules and the subject-expert's finite weekly review capacity.

Provide source-attributed correspondence and interview extracts covering the informal delivery promise, contract manager concern, failed review threads, incomplete asset receipts and operating constraints.
Provide the project-specific England and Scotland release requirements, including their required sequence and owners, without requiring internet research.
Provide contractual definitions for both review-copy delivery and accepted-master delivery, because stakeholder language uses the word delivery ambiguously.

imperfections_to_seed: Historical evidence must show eleven late modules among fourteen completed modules.
All four suspected causes must be facially plausible from isolated records.
The single subject-expert approval queue must be the recurring critical-path cause across the late pattern.
Incomplete assets must affect some modules but be resolved within available float or before they become the controlling delay.
Block-booked colour grading must amplify delay after late approval for some modules but not explain the initial recurring slip.
Dropped review threads must create an audit and rework risk while the timestamps show that reconstructed comments did not cause the recurring contractual variance.
The informal promise must be earlier than the fully compliant accepted-master forecast under available capacity and must lack formal baseline authorization.
At least one future handoff must be marked unconfirmed so a competent schedule must expose an exception path rather than treating every input as certain.
gold_relationships: Historical variance equals actual chosen delivery milestone minus the corresponding contractual baseline using the supplied business-day calendar.
The late count is based on distinct completed modules whose actual chosen delivery milestone falls after baseline; duplicated source excerpts do not create additional modules.
Critical-path attribution follows the activity chain: a condition is causal only where its delay consumes available float and moves the chosen delivery milestone.
The primary cause is the subject-expert approval queue because approval waiting repeatedly consumes float and propagates to downstream dates across the late modules.
Future earliest feasible dates are derived from supplied durations, finish-to-start dependencies, jurisdiction gates, working calendars, approval capacity and colour-grade booking availability.
A schedule may use review copy or accepted master as delivery, but every variance, promise comparison, service-credit implication and final date must use the selected definition consistently.
No client commitment is valid solely because it appears in informal correspondence; formal commitment status follows the authorization evidence in the source.
Mandatory editorial, accessibility, jurisdiction and acceptance gates cannot be removed to achieve the informal promise.
A compliant exception path holds or relabels incomplete work, preserves the issue record, names an escalation owner and reforecasts or routes the change through documented control.
acceptable_solver_readings: Treat delivery as issue of the client review copy and present the resulting schedule as an internal forecast, provided all labels and variance calculations use that milestone.

Treat delivery as acceptance of the final master and present the resulting schedule as an internal forecast or formally supportable commitment, provided the source supports the chosen status and all calculations remain consistent.
reference_solution_verification: Generate a DOCX containing a concise variance narrative, causal finding, integrated schedule, jurisdiction treatment and exception controls.
Recalculate all historical and future dates from the workbook using Python business-day logic and compare them with the reference document at a tolerance of 0 business days.
Render the DOCX offline with LibreOffice, confirm that it is no more than five pages and inspect it at normal zoom for table clipping and readability.
Walk every rubric item against the rendered reference solution and the supplied workbook, including both permissible interpretations of delivery.

reference_files.purpose: Consolidated source for historical module timestamps, future work, baseline milestones, calendars, bookings, correspondence, interview evidence, contractual definitions and England and Scotland release requirements.
reference_files.discovery: Open the workbook and review its consolidated project records, source extracts and stated scheduling assumptions.

deliverables.description: A presentation-ready re-baselined delivery schedule and variance memo for the operations team.
constraints: Write the file at the top level of the working directory.
Do not exceed five rendered pages.
Use only figures and commitments supported by the supplied evidence.
Cover both England and Scotland release paths.
Present one explicit interpretation of delivery and use it consistently.
Present facts and an executable schedule without making a recommendation.
